hook: North China gneiss dated to 3.95 billion years hints at a brief subduction event in the Hadean
hook_turn: hints at a brief subduction event in the Hadean
summary: Zircon in a gneiss from Hebei records oxygen and hafnium signatures of altered crust that was buried deep (above 1.6 GPa) along a cool path. That points to a transient subduction event, only the second known rock above 3.9 billion years. The subduction reading comes from modeling and one rock unit.
title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks.
